messages:
Maria Gomez: Quick sync — we need to finalize how we surface routing fallbacks in the API and Console. Two open axes: HTTP status/signature and Console badging + telemetry labels.
Samir Patel: Agreed. Primary requirement: clients must be able to deterministically detect a fallback vs a hard failure. That drives retry/adaptive logic.
AJ: For detectability, a distinct status code + structured header seems simplest. E.g. 200 + X-Redwood-Fallback=variant is not great because 200 implies success/quality.
Frank Lee: Right. If we return 200 when we downgraded model, SDKs will silently accept lower-quality output. We should prefer a 2xx vs 5xx tradeoff: maybe 200 with a non-hidden warning header AND a telemetry flag? Or a 503-like soft-fallback status?
Maria Gomez: My concern with 4xx/5xx is that many customers treat non-2xx as terminal and will fail the request early instead of showing degraded UI. Fallbacks are graceful degradations — they should be apparent but not treated as crash.
Samir Patel: Proposal A: Keep 200 for success when fallback served, but include: `X-Redwood-Fallback: <variant>` and `X-Redwood-Fallback-Score: <0-1>` plus `Warning` header with short message. SDKs would surface a structured field in response object. Telemetry gets a boolean tag fallback=true.
AJ: Proposal B: Use 2xx for success but attach `X-Redwood-Exposure: fallback` and add `X-Redwood-Client-Hint: retryable` only if fallback triggered due to capacity, not quality. That way clients can choose to prompt user or automatically requeue.
Nina: Could we instead use a 207 Multi-Status? Kinda hacky and will confuse clients. I'd avoid nonstandard codes.
Frank Lee: Another angle: Console UX — we need distinct badges on Routes and Model dashboards: "fallback rate", "fallback latency delta", and a linked list of recent fallback events with reasons (capacity vs routing policy vs model failover). That helps SREs diagnose if fallback is expected.
Maria Gomez: Telemetry contract: add `fallback_reason` label: values = [capacity, policy, model_error, degraded_quality]. Also record `fallback_variant` and `original_model`. Those must be searchable in Console flows.
Samir Patel: For quota vs throttle: if request is rate-limited, return 429 + `Retry-After`. If we redirect to a lower-tier model because quota exceeded for the premium model, that's a fallback (not a throttle). So 429 remains for throttles.
AJ: Edge case: Can we allow 206 Partial Content? No — misleading. Keep it simple: 200 + explicit headers and structured SDK field. But console and alerts must treat fallback rates as high-severity if they exceed thresholds.
Nina: SDK responsibilities: expose `response.fallback` object when present and emit an event `redwood.fallback` to the telemetry pipeline. Document clear guidance for customers: show banner, offer "try again with premium" button, or log for offline processing.
Frank Lee: Rollout plan: start with header-only beta for a week (no SDK changes). After collecting telemetry, ship SDK update that unwraps the header into `response.fallback`. Beta routes flagged in Console with a yellow badge.
Maria Gomez: UX copy for console badge: "Fallbacks: X% — showing degraded/alternate model". Add drilldown to list sample prompts + returned variant. Also allow toggling alerting thresholds.
Samir Patel: Action items: 1) eng-platform draft HTTP header names + example responses (AJ). 2) telemetry schema update PR with labels and ranges (Frank). 3) SDK spec doc and beta timeline (Nina). 4) Console badging mockups (Maria).
AJ: I'll draft the header spec today: example: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Fallback: model-small-v2
X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: capacity
X-Redwood-Fallback-Quality: 0.73
Warning: 199 Redwood "served fallback model-small-v2 due to capacity"`
Nina: I'll start the SDK doc and share a short changelog entry for customers.
deploy-bot: deploy queued to staging: infra/service-routing v2.3.4 — changelist includes fallback header support (no SDK changes).
Maria Gomez: Perfect. We'll reconvene after staging telemetry is in (check back in 48h). Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
